title: Restricted Sumset Problem
exact_target: Can every sufficiently large finite set of integers provide a subset of size at least the hundredth power of its logarithmic size such that no sum of two distinct chosen elements belongs to the original set?

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 93 (GREEN-002). CC BY 4.0.

Adrian Beker, \emph{The Erdős--Moser sum-free set problem via improved bounds for $k$-configurations}, arXiv:2501.10203v2, 2 October 2026, section 1, pp. 1--3: sum-free-with-respect-to-$A$ definition and explicit identification of Green's Problem 2. The catalogue specifies the target exponent $100$; the paper's proved lower bound in Theorem 1.2 has exponent $1+c$.
Ben Green, \emph{100 Open Problems}, author manuscript with December 2025 updates, Problem 2, pp. 3--4.
